\"You don't love me.\"
\"I want a fur coat.\"
\"Let's go visit my mom.\"
\"Give me some money.\"
\"I gave you the best years of my life.\"
\"My mom was right about you.\"

The home screen should feature an image of a bored-looking wife.
Next to it, there should be a button that, when pressed, triggers one of the listed phrases at random.

Built a complete, responsive Russian-language family simulator in `index.html`.

- The home screen features an original illustrated, bored-looking wife and a button that speaks a random phrase in Russian.
- The phrase menu includes all six requested lines, translated into Russian, and lets you add or remove custom phrases. Custom phrases persist in the browser.
- Added a repeat button, turn counter, and on-screen fallback if speech synthesis isn’t available.

Assumption: phrases are spoken with the browser’s Russian text-to-speech voice, if available. I verified the JavaScript syntax and that the page serves successfully. I couldn’t check a screenshot because Chromium isn’t installed in this environment.
